front: What was the Covenant of the League of Nations?
back: The founding document of the League, part of the Treaty of Versailles, setting out its rules, including collective security (Article 10) and sanctions (Article 16).
The idea that all members act together against any aggressor, so that no state can attack another without facing the combined strength of the rest.
Decisions in the League's Council and Assembly needed the agreement of all members present, so any member could block action.

front: When did the League begin work, and where?
back: 10 January 1920, in Geneva; the first Assembly met on 15 November 1920.
Japan invaded after the Mukden incident (18 September 1931); the League's Lytton Commission condemned it, and Japan left the League in 1933.
Italy invaded on 3 October 1935; the League imposed weak sanctions without oil; the Hoare-Laval plan leaked; Addis Ababa fell in May 1936.

front: What were the League's main humanitarian successes?
back: Returning prisoners of war, helping refugees (Nansen passport), health and anti-slavery work, and the International Labour Organization.
No USA, no army, unanimity, self-interest of Britain and France, the Depression and the aggression of dictators.

front: Why was the Abyssinian crisis significant for Africans?
back: Abyssinia was an independent African state that had defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896, and the League's failure to defend it was seen as a betrayal.
